forces.title: Higher financing costs and geopolitical risks cap growth
forces.description: Elevated financing costs, driven by rising interest rates, continue to be a significant headwind for the European construction sector. Alongside this, ongoing geopolitical risks contribute to broader economic uncertainty, dampening investment appetite and capping overall growth momentum. These factors collectively make both residential and commercial projects less viable and slow down market activity across the region.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Weak building sector due to high costs and uncertainty
forces.description: The residential and non-residential building sector remains a weak spot in Europe's construction landscape. High interest rates, coupled with persistently high construction costs, make new property investments less attractive for households and businesses. Economic uncertainty further exacerbates this caution, leading to subdued demand and a slowdown in new building projects, hindering the overall recovery of the construction sector.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Infrastructure investment driven by EU funds and network expansion
forces.description: Infrastructure investment continues to be a positive driver for the European construction sector, providing a significant offset against various headwinds. This growth is substantially supported by targeted EU funds and increased spending on crucial energy and digital networks. These investments enable large-scale projects, such as upgrades to power infrastructure for energy transition and expansion of fibre-optic and 5G networks, contributing to stable demand for construction services.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Difficulty passing rising input costs to customers
forces.description: Construction companies across Europe face increasing challenges in passing higher input costs, such as energy-intensive materials, through the value chain to end-buyers. Governments, non-residential investors, and homebuyers are already grappling with higher interest rates, limiting their capacity to absorb further cost increases. This pressure on contractors' ability to adjust pricing exacerbates margin erosion and increases the risk of disputes, delays, or halted projects, especially under existing contract terms.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Higher energy prices boost demand for energy-efficient homes
forces.description: Rising energy prices are reinforcing the value premium for energy-efficient homes, encouraging greater investment in insulation, high-performance glazing, and more efficient heating systems. This trend shortens payback periods for such investments and is expected to sustain demand for energy-efficient properties. Stricter renovation standards further incentivize buyers to consider future renovation costs, making energy performance a crucial determinant of property value and marketability.
forces.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

forces.title: Low construction activity dampens growth across sectors
forces.description: Low construction activity in Norway, characterized by few new residential and commercial projects, is broadly dampening economic growth. This directly affects order volumes for related commercial services, such as architectural firms and technical consultants. While some regions show isolated pickups, the overall sentiment indicates a significant headwind, with many contacts reporting that the anticipated upturn in residential construction is continually being delayed.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

forces.title: Data centre buildout and defense spending boost manufacturing
forces.description: Increased data centre buildout and higher defense spending are acting as significant tailwinds for domestically oriented manufacturing in Norway. This trend is boosting demand for energy supply equipment, including cables, transformers, and switchboards, impacting a growing number of firms. Moreover, continued investment in defense, security, and preparedness is lifting activity for manufacturers in both domestic and export markets, providing a crucial growth impetus.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

forces.title: Infrastructure growth slowed by costs, staff shortages, regulations
forces.description: The robust growth rate in the Dutch infrastructure sector is decelerating due to several significant headwinds. High construction costs, persistent staff shortages, and stringent nitrogen restrictions are limiting project execution. Additionally, constrained government budgets, which are prioritizing maintenance over new construction, further impede new development. These factors collectively contribute to a slowdown despite production levels remaining significantly higher than five years ago.
forces.source_title: Dutch housing permits hit 10-year high, but construction still slow off the…

forces.title: Cost inflation, staff shortages, and delivery times remain risks
forces.description: Irish construction firms face persistent challenges from cost inflation, which impacts project budgets and profitability. Alongside this, ongoing staff shortages limit capacity and project timelines. Lengthening delivery times for materials and components add further complexity and risk, potentially causing delays and cost overruns. These factors require firms to build flexibility into contracts, stress-test project margins, and carefully manage supply chain relationships to mitigate financial exposure.

forces.title: AI to automate nonphysical work, reshape AEC industry leadership
forces.description: Artificial Intelligence is poised to fundamentally restructure the Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) industry by automating a significant portion of nonphysical work. This shift will likely redefine industry leadership, favoring firms that rapidly adapt and integrate AI into core operations. While AI may not lead to an 'extinction event,' it will drive substantial changes in workflows, decision-making, and competitive advantage, with up to 50% of nonphysical work in architecture/engineering and 39% in construction having automation potential.
forces.source_title: How AI is reshaping the future of the AEC industry

forces.title: Value shifts to firms controlling project data and outcomes
forces.description: The emergence of agentic AI is fundamentally altering how value and profit are captured in the AEC sector. A lasting competitive advantage will accrue to firms that effectively control proprietary project data, manage the workflows where critical decisions are made, and can shift their commercial models to charge for outcomes rather than simply labor hours. This represents a significant structural change, rewarding data-driven and outcome-focused business models.
forces.source_title: How AI is reshaping the future of the AEC industry

forces.title: AI enables BIM to become a live, continuously updated project view
forces.description: AI is set to transform Building Information Modeling (BIM) from a static, end-of-project file into a dynamic, continuously updated view throughout a project's lifecycle. This structural change will enable automated tracking of installed materials, real-time project progress, schedule risk, and performance, significantly reducing reliance on manual field reporting. Such integration will enhance efficiency, accuracy, and decision-making by providing comprehensive, up-to-date project intelligence.
forces.source_title: How AI is reshaping the future of the AEC industry

forces.title: AI use requires robust governance, audit trails, human oversight
forces.description: As AI integrates into AEC workflows, practical limits and formal regulations will increasingly demand robust governance. Companies will need clear records of how AI was utilized, the data it accessed, applied checks and controls, and documented human reviews or approvals. Professional engineering bodies are updating conduct codes, mandating AI use proportional to risk. Audit trails, human oversight, and strong AI governance will become essential for winning and maintaining client trust and mitigating liability.
forces.source_title: How AI is reshaping the future of the AEC industry

forces.title: Metals, machinery, electrotechnical industry benefit from electrification
forces.description: Parts of the Dutch metals, machinery, and electrotechnical industry are experiencing a structural benefit from global trends such as the rise of semiconductors, increased electrification, and higher defense spending. This creates sustained demand for specialized components, equipment, and manufacturing services, providing a counterweight to broader economic uncertainty. This shift highlights a widening divide between benefiting sectors and those under pressure from energy-intensive basic industries.
forces.source_title: Dutch manufacturing set for a faster rebound than its eurozone peers

forces.title: Postponed residential construction due to high rates and costs
forces.description: The pickup in Norwegian residential construction is continually being postponed, primarily due to the prevailing high interest rates and persistent expectations of further increases in building costs. This financial burden makes new housing projects less viable for developers and less affordable for buyers, leading to project delays and cancellations. This acts as a significant headwind, undermining growth in the construction sector and related services.

viewpoints.title: Europe's construction sector faces weak growth amidst stabilizing volumes
viewpoints.description: Europe's construction volumes are expected to grow marginally by 0.5% in 2026, following a 1.8% decline in 2024 and 2.3% growth in 2025. This modest growth is driven by infrastructure investment and Germany's gradual rebound, but is capped by higher financing costs, increased geopolitical risks, and a subdued residential sector. The overall sector has lagged broader GDP growth, with confidence indicators weakening in late 2025.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

viewpoints.title: Building sector remains weak; infrastructure provides positive offset
viewpoints.description: The building sector, encompassing both residential and non-residential construction, continues to be a weak point across Europe. This weakness stems from elevated interest rates, high construction costs, and general economic uncertainty, leading households and businesses to be more hesitant about new property investments. Conversely, infrastructure investment, bolstered by EU funds and spending on energy and digital networks, stands out as a positive driver, partly offsetting the sector's headwinds.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

viewpoints.title: Germany's construction sector poised for modest recovery after contraction
viewpoints.description: Germany's construction sector, Europe’s largest market, is anticipated to return to growth in 2026 after five consecutive years of contraction, during which it shrank by over 10% between 2020 and 2025. The recovery is expected to be modest initially, gradually gaining momentum into 2027, with support primarily coming from the housing and infrastructure segments. This marks a positive cyclical rebound within a challenging broader European context.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

viewpoints.title: French construction faces significant contraction despite policy support
viewpoints.description: France’s construction output experienced a 3.5% decline in 2025, followed by further quarter-on-quarter contractions in early 2026. The sector's confidence has weakened, and housing permits remain below previous year levels. Combined with sluggish GDP growth, this points to a projected 2.5% contraction in 2026. Despite the expansion of a zero-interest mortgage scheme for new-build homes, the policy has yet to gain significant traction, contributing to a challenging outlook.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

viewpoints.title: Spain's construction sector continues recovery, supported by GDP growth
viewpoints.description: Spain’s construction sector is in a recovery phase, having lost over 25% of its output between 2019 and 2022 before rebounding in 2023. Forecasts suggest a 3% growth in 2026. While building permits have shown a sharp increase in recent years, their momentum is easing. Contractor confidence is also moderating from previously high levels. Nevertheless, robust GDP growth is expected to provide ongoing support for construction activity this year and next.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

viewpoints.title: Dutch construction to stabilise, infrastructure remains key driver
viewpoints.description: The Netherlands' construction output is expected to stabilise in 2026 following a weak first half, with modest growth projected for 2027. Housing construction should gradually recover as increased building permits translate into starts and completions, though project delays and limited grid capacity may constrain the pace. Infrastructure remains a crucial growth driver for the sector. Total production contracted by 1% in Q1 and Q2 2026, lagging the wider Dutch economy.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

viewpoints.title: Belgian housing market shows resilience but faces weakening momentum
viewpoints.description: The Belgian housing market displayed unexpected resilience in Q2 2026, with a slight increase in prices and a recovery in transactions. However, underlying indicators suggest a more challenging outlook. Weaker mortgage production and persistently high interest rates are expected to dampen demand momentum in coming quarters. ING Research forecasts nominal median house price increases to slow to 2.5% in 2026 and 2.0% in 2027, following a return to positive real price growth in 2025.
viewpoints.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

viewpoints.title: Norwegian construction activity remains low, residential upturn delayed
viewpoints.description: Construction activity in Norway is currently low, with few new residential and commercial projects initiating. The anticipated upturn in residential construction continues to be delayed, leading to a dampening effect on order volumes for related commercial services like architects and technical consultants. While state-level projects are increasing, municipal construction projects are fewer, contributing to a weak overall sentiment, particularly in regions like Central where demand for housing remains low.
viewpoints.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

viewpoints.title: Irish construction strengthens with broad-based recovery and rising employment
viewpoints.description: Irish construction activity is showing robust signs of strengthening, marking a third consecutive month of growth driven by sustained new order inflows. The recovery is broad-based across the sector, with commercial construction demonstrating the strongest growth, and civil engineering activity reaching its highest level since 2022. Employment within the sector is also rising, indicating healthy underlying momentum. Despite this, housing remains the weakest segment, though strong underlying demand is expected to provide long-term support.

viewpoints.title: AI set to rewire AEC industry, offering significant value and competitive advantage
viewpoints.description: Artificial Intelligence is poised to fundamentally transform the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) sector, creating substantial value for early adopters. Firms that quickly reimagine workflows, leverage data effectively, and automate work sites are expected to thrive. While not an 'extinction event,' AI will reshape industry leadership. Initial productivity gains from design and modeling workflows are becoming table stakes, pushing firms to integrate AI into end-to-end processes for sustained competitive advantage, potentially unlocking billions in annual value by 2030.
viewpoints.source_title: How AI is reshaping the future of the AEC industry

viewpoints.title: Norwegian construction profitability remains weak despite modest improvements
viewpoints.description: Profitability in the Norwegian construction sector continues to be weak, exacerbated by fierce competition for contracts. However, there has been a modest improvement for some contacts, attributed to slightly higher activity levels and better cost control. The completion of unprofitable fixed-price contracts, which were entered into before construction costs sharply increased, has also contributed to improved margins for specific firms, providing a cautious positive outlook amidst overall sector challenges.
